user.title: New scenario
user.description: Add one scenario per setup you want to compare.

data_description.name: e.g. '16 kWh + 6 kWp'. Each scenario is its own virtual battery, so you can compare setups side by side.
data_description.copy_from: Optional: start from an existing scenario's entities and settings.

data_description.tariff_preset: Pick a starting point; live rate entities override these.

hardware_preset.title: Hardware preset
hardware_preset.description: Overwrites the hardware numbers with the preset's values.

data_description.hardware_preset: Pick a starting point; every value stays editable afterwards.

sources_live.title: Live data
sources_live.description: All optional. The twin works from the tariff and a typical profile without them.

data_description.power_entity: Whole-home import power sensor, W or kW. Used to drive the live twin.
data_description.ev_power_entities: Optional. Lets the twin separate EV load from house load, so the battery never 'feeds' a car.
data_description.pv_now_entity: Real-time expected/forecast solar power sensor (W or kW), for the array size set below. Overrides the hourly forecast for the current slot.
data_description.import_now_entity: Current tariff price entity (GBP/kWh or p/kWh, auto-detected).
data_description.export_now_entity: Current export tariff price entity (GBP/kWh or p/kWh).

sources_octopus.title: Octopus Energy
sources_octopus.description: Entities from the Octopus Energy integration, or your own.

data_description.import_rates_entities: Octopus Energy integration rate entities (current day + next day). Their 'rates' attribute is read.
data_description.export_rates_entities: Octopus export rate entities, if you want real export prices (e.g. Agile Outgoing).
data_description.dispatch_entity: Octopus Intelligent 'dispatching' binary sensor - planned smart-charge slots are priced at the cheap rate.
data_description.power_up_entity: Any binary sensor / event / calendar that is 'on' or lists windows during Power Up events.
data_description.power_down_entity: Any binary sensor / event / calendar that is 'on' or lists windows during Power Down events.

data.history_days: Days of history to learn from

data_description.forecast_device: Pick your Forecast.Solar device - that is all. Its sensors and array size are found automatically. Leave blank to auto-use it if it is the only one installed.
data_description.forecast_ref_kwp: Optional. Normally read from the Forecast.Solar device. The twin scales that array to the one you are modelling.
data_description.forecast_scale_pct: 100 = trust the forecast. Lower (e.g. 85) makes the planner assume less sun than forecast, so it charges more overnight.
data_description.consumption_stat: Long-term statistic id for whole-home import kWh (an energy sensor, or e.g. octopus_energy:electricity_<serial>_<mpan>_import_consumption - see Developer tools > Statistics).
data_description.ev_stats: Comma-separated statistic ids for your chargers' kWh. If blank, off-peak demand above the night base load is assumed to be the cars.

data_description.inverter_kw: Clips solar and caps battery power (hybrid inverter assumption).
data_description.pv_annual_yield: From PVGIS or your installer for your roof. UK south-facing is ~900-1000.
data_description.export_limit_kw: 3.68 kW is the G98 single-phase default.
data_description.cycle_cost_p: Optional. Makes the planner avoid low-value cycling.

sources_heat.title: Heat pump data
sources_heat.description: Gas history and outdoor temperature let the twin work out how much of your gas is heating and how much is hot water.

data_description.gas_stat: Statistic id of your gas kWh (the Octopus gas consumption sensor). Used to split hot water from heating.
data_description.outdoor_temp_entity: Used to fit gas use against weather, and to nudge the forecast.
data_description.outdoor_temp_stat: Optional. Statistic id with temperature history. Blank = use the sensor above.
data_description.weather_entity: Optional. Gives the planner the real forecast instead of a seasonal curve.
data_description.tank_temp_entity: Optional. If you have a real tank sensor it overrides the model.

supply.title: Supply & main fuse
supply.description: Limits how much the planner draws from the grid (cars + heat pump + battery charging).

data_description.main_fuse_a: Typically 100 A for a single-phase UK home; older homes can be 60-80 A.
data_description.fuse_usable_pct: The planner keeps grid import below this share of the fuse rating.

data.hp_enabled: Model a heat pump + induction hob

data_description.hp_enabled: Replaces the gas combi (heating and hot water) and gas hob.
data_description.legionella_c: Set to the set point to switch off.
data_description.dhw_start: Main tank charge, inside the cheap window. It also tops up during Power Up and smart-charge slots.
data_description.hp_capacity_kw: Undersized on cold days = resistive backup, shown as a higher bill.
data_description.flow_temp_c: Lower is better: ~35 underfloor, 45 good radiators, 55+ old radiators.
data_description.base_temp_c: Outdoor temperature below which heating is needed.

data_description.boiler_eff_dhw: Lower than heating: combis lose a lot on short draws.
data_description.induction_ratio: ~0.5: induction is roughly twice as efficient.
data_description.fallback_annual_gas_kwh: Used until enough gas + temperature history exists.
data_description.gas_disconnect: Counts the avoided standing charge as a saving.
data_description.hp_grant: e.g. the Boiler Upgrade Scheme - check current eligibility and amount.

data_description.cheap_p: Used when no rate entity covers a slot.
data_description.power_up_import_p: Placeholder - set to the actual terms of the event.
data_description.power_down_export_p: Placeholder - set to the actual terms of the event.
data_description.power_down_bonus_p: Extra reward per kWh the battery discharges during an event.

data_description.inverter_kw: Clips solar and caps battery power (hybrid inverter assumption).
data_description.pv_annual_yield: From PVGIS or your installer for your roof. UK south-facing is ~900-1000.
data_description.export_limit_kw: 3.68 kW is the G98 single-phase default.
data_description.cycle_cost_p: Optional. Makes the planner avoid low-value cycling.

data_description.other_cost: Scaffolding, consumer unit, EV-safe isolation, etc.

data_description.export_margin_p: Export only if it beats re-buying at the cheap rate by this much.
data_description.arbitrage: Charge from the cheap window specifically to export later.

data_description.night_base_load_kw: Used to separate cars from house when no EV statistics are given.

vehicles.title: Vehicles

vehicle_add.title: Vehicle
vehicle_add.description: Pick the car's **device** and give it a mode - that is usually all you need. Charge target comes from the car's own charge limit when it has one.

data_description.device_id: Pick the car's device (e.g. your Tesla). Its battery, charger power, plugged-in, location, charge-limit and energy entities are found automatically. The fields below only override or add to that - or fill them all in for a car with no device.
data_description.target_soc_entity: Optional. e.g. a Tesla's charge-limit number. When present it is used as the charge target instead of the fixed value below.
data_description.name: Optional if you picked a device (its name is used). Used to label the car on the dashboard.
data_description.mode: Only one car per account is usually on Intelligent Octopus Go. The other charges on the off-peak schedule.
data_description.power_entity: Optional. W or kW from the car or charger integration. Lets the twin see real charging and learn session sizes.
data_description.plug_entity: Optional. A binary sensor, or a charging-status sensor - states like on/off, connected/disconnected, charging, stopped are understood.
data_description.home_entity: Optional. A device tracker / person / binary sensor. Any zone other than 'home' counts as away.
data_description.soc_entity: Optional. With it the twin knows exactly how much the car still needs.
data_description.session_kwh: 0 = learn it from observed sessions. Used when the car has no battery-level entity.
data_description.energy_stat: Optional. Long-term kWh statistic of this car's charging, so the twin can learn its pattern from history straight away.
data_description.plug_states: Only if your integration uses unusual wording. Comma-separated, e.g. 'ready,charging'. Blank = auto-detect.
